questions.question: What makes a unit test valuable?
questions.title: Why Testing
questions.direct_answer: A valuable unit test is fast, deterministic, isolated from external systems, and asserts observable behavior rather than implementation details.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you understand Why Testing beyond memorized syntax.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Giving a definition without explaining a practical trade-off.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Connect the concept to a small production example and state its complexity or failure mode.

sections.title: What the interviewer wants
sections.content: Give a plain definition of Why Testing, explain why it matters, and show that you know one limitation. Keep the answer tied to the problem rather than listing jargon.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content: A valuable unit test is fast, deterministic, isolated from external systems, and asserts observable behavior rather than implementation details. In a real project, I would use it when it fits the situation and mention one edge case.

sections.title: Concept explained
sections.content: Start with a small example of Why Testing. Then walk through what changes step by step, compare it with the simplest alternative, and finish with the trade-off. A good check is a focused test for the normal case, an empty or invalid input, and the largest expected input.
